claim_boundary: Prospective development-only quality-frontier contract. It does not authorize production pretraining, held-out test access, a biological-improvement claim, or a cross-paper SOTA claim. Every comparison must be rerun on the same frozen examples, mappings, candidate sets, metrics, and bootstrap units.

compute_optimality.research_basis: Protein MLM scaling exhibits data-repeat overfitting and benefits from diverse metagenomic data; the fitted compute-optimal frontier scales model size faster than training tokens, so this project freezes its useful-token budget and measures quality instead of assuming a generic text-LLM tokens-per-parameter rule.

msa_pairformer_111m.role: contact-quality and quality-per-GPU-hour baseline; not a scale proxy

plm_interact_650m.role: objective ablation reference only; its random-negative semantics are not inherited

pplm_650m.role: checkpoint-compatible pair-MLM reference; contact use requires a separately audited head and identical-split rerun

research_warning.finding: Pretrained protein language models can leak information into downstream PPI inference and inflate evaluation scores; current PPI methods also remain weak on OOD and mutation-sensitivity tests.

stage_a_objective_sequence.name: pair_balanced_masked_language_modeling
stage_a_objective_sequence.purpose: learn pair-conditioned sequence representations at scale without asserting that an unobserved pair is a biological noninteraction

stage_a_objective_sequence.name: cognate_retrieval_with_matched_partner_swaps
stage_a_objective_sequence.purpose: prove partner dependence while limiting shortcut and false-negative claims

stage_a_objective_sequence.name: pair_contact_specialization
stage_a_objective_sequence.purpose: learn residue-pair geometry without using development or held-out test labels

development_quality_frontier.promotion_rule: ABPairFM 3B must improve the frozen same-contract development frontier over the ESM2-3B control and must report its delta and GPU-hour cost versus both 650M and 111M pair-aware baselines. A larger parameter count, lower training loss, or author-reported cross-paper number is insufficient.
